title: The Winter Compass
premise: In 1747, mapmaker's apprentice Beatrix Thornbury completes the atlas her master died for, only to discover his final charts contain evidence that a celebrated naval victory was built on a deliberate wrecking of allied ships — and that her master's 'death' was murder. When Aldous Vane, a disgraced clerk carrying letters in the master's unmistakable hand, arrives seeking her help, they must race to place the truth before the Admiralty ahead of the victors' historians, who are already burning archives. Betrayed by the patron who funded the atlas, Beatrix chooses truth over the belonging she has spent ten years earning, testifying at cost of her name and livelihood. The atlas is published with an appendix of correction, the master posthumously vindicated, and Beatrix leaves London to chart coastlines no power has yet claimed.
about_author: Emrys Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing eighteenth-century maritime charts before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal cottage where the tide, they insist, keeps better time than any clock.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Coast
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Finishing her dead master's atlas in the workshop that has been her only home for ten years, Beatrix discovers a hidden folio of charts contradicting the official account of the Battle of Corren Sound. That night, Aldous Vane arrives soaked and desperate, carrying letters in her master's living handwriting. Emotional beat: the shock of learning the silences she mastered were walls around a crime.

chapters.title: Letters from a Drowned Man
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Beatrix and Aldous. Aldous reveals he served as the master's secret copyist and witnessed the falsified logs; together they decode the atlas's marginalia into a chain of evidence. But Beatrix's patron, Sir Edmund Halloway — funder of the atlas and architect of the cover-up — summons her, offering partnership if the folio burns. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into temptation as belonging is weaponized.

chapters.title: The Burning Archive
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Halloway's men raid the workshop; the master's original letters burn while Beatrix and Aldous flee with only the decoded charts and one surviving letter. Hunted through frozen streets, they reach a sympathetic naval chaplain willing to enter their testimony into the Admiralty record before Halloway's historians file the sanitized version at dawn. Emotional beat: terror and resolve fused — the point of no return.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In the Admiralty chamber, Beatrix presents the charts and names Halloway, sacrificing the atlas commission and her place in the guild. Halloway falls as the true record enters history; the atlas publishes months later with her appendix of correction. She declines a rebuilt career in London and departs to survey unmapped northern coasts, Aldous at her side. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into freedom — truth chosen over safety, at last without regret.
